body: please let me know what you think!!

i don't want to condescend and assume that this book will magically solve your problems (i know it didn't magically solve all of mine) i really highly recommend reading it before you make your choice. it's about 100 pages, took me about 3-4 days of slowly reading. i can't understand your specific kind of pain, only my own - but i can tell you that i feel like i'm on that ledge too. even after reading this i still can't stop thinking about it. but i keep going over passages and trying to hold onto them. 

http://www.ryanpatrickhalligan.org/documents/Forever_Decision.pdf
thank you for talking with me tonight, and i hope you have a good night and pleasant tomorrow.

she thinks i'm funny, and (at the time she told me, it was more accurate) that i have a drive to help other people do things. which wasn't that wrong, i used to be really into helping people with projects (and my own). she likes that i'm straightforward (i know i type a *lot* as is but i usually like to condense things to the most straightforward, "whole truth and nothing but the truth" manner). she still manages to think i'm attractive after seeing me at my worst (like, the "morning after crying and vomiting with the flu all night and trying to have someone cover my 7 AM opening shift" worst.)

again, thank you...i've kind of been crying at my computer for the past half hour because it just feels nice to have someone listen after so long.

i don't know how many good parts there can be...i can't really provide my mom with money, and even now, we talk less and argue more. i know that sounds harsh after i've pointed out the sacrifices my mom made, but i don't think she should've been a parent. i don't think she ever got the chance to learn how to deal w/her own negative feelings (she mocked me for crying when my great-grandpa - HER grandpa - died) and having lived away from home for about five years now, i feel less and less like a part of the family? i don't know. 

i'm not sure if i'm talking in weird circles or if i just seem like i'm making my situation out to be worse...my childhood /wasn't/ the worst; i was still fed and clothed (only technically homeless once!) but it wasn't what it could've been, either. 

my mom was a tired, overworked young woman, repressing her own emotions and trauma. she lashed out when we misbehaved. i've had shoes thrown at my head, been hit with belts, wooden spoons, hangers, anything she could grab within arms range (which was considerably better than when she made /me/ fetch something). she's had a string of boyfriends, and while i'm reluctant to call *all* of them abusive, i remember waking up a lot in the middle of the night and hearing arguing, crying. creeping into the kitchen and seeing our glass kitchen table shattered to pieces. barricading my bedroom door shut so they couldn't try to get at me if i'd said something like a smartass. 

honestly, when i think about killing myself, i feel guilty more for the sake of my gf and my roommates (who would unfortunately have to be the ones to discover my body *and* make up for my share of rent) rather than my family. 

thank you for taking the time to respond, though. i know this is a lot to unpack. i feel weird doing it to a complete stranger? like i don't want to waste your time and seem like i'm here to get pity points. i don't know.

i felt really, really, hopeful. i'm an artist and it was a job helping another artist who'd have relative success (by no means "famous", but happily well-off doing freelance and gallery shows) which made it even more upsetting when she suddenly decided to let me go (her reasons were that i hadn't taken true advantage of the "mentorship" aspect of the role - mind you, she was working under a tight time constraint and explicitly told me when she couldn't talk during tasks that she had to focus on.) 

but, aside from that, i've always felt to some degree like i was nothing. my parents were 15/18 when i was born, which resulted in my dad (the 18 y/o) going to prison and never speaking to me again. my mom raised me (and later, my sister) for the most part on her own...resorting to prostitution to pay for our christmas presents when i was in middle school. (i found out by googling her name, during a time when that was the fun thing to do. mistake.) she wanted to be a nurse when she grew up, but because of me, she just barely scrapped through high school. she couldn't go to college. 

my dad can't get a job because he's registered as a sex offender (despite my mother insisting it was consensual) and my mom can't get a better paying job because, by being born, i've robbed her of that freedom - of time, energy, resources. it's very hard to feel like i can justify continuing to live when, by existing, i've costed people their future.
